Recent comparisons have shown that SAR values may overestimate ESP values in drill hole material, so SAR values should be interpreted with caution. Alkali intervals have been identified on both tracts, although such materials are most evident in the Tract III interburden, and in some cases the material immediately above the Rosebud-McKay coal seam. Samples from some holes were analyzed using the ESP procedure, while the SAR procedure was used for the majority of sodium analysis. Where ESP values are available, most interburden samples were in the range of 10-25, with many values below 10 and one value exceeding 30. SAR values of interburden in several holes in the vicinity of the existing mine were in the range of 20-40 with one value exceeding 50. In contrast, SAR values of interval samples from several holes on Tract III did not exceed 10. Based on available SAR and ESP values, alkali interburden intervals were present in 18 of 38 Tract III holes and two of 11 Tract II holes. Alkali materials may be present on the surface after regrading, particularly in some areas of Tract III.
At the request of Westmoreland Resources, the Colorado School of Mines Research Institute conducted comparative SAR and ESP analyses, and clay mineralogy studies on selected overburden and interburden samples from Hole 640, a centrally located hole on Tract III. The results are presented in Appendix C. Without exception, SAR values were higher than ESP values.
